Text: $NFLX reports Q3 earnings next Tuesday… Here’s what investors should be expecting: Revenue: $12.86B, +11.7% YoY Operating income: $4.27B, +31% YoY Operating margin: 33.2% vs. 28.2% last year EPS: $0.82 vs. $0.59 last year Those are basically right in line with where Wall Street is sitting heading into the report. Management also expects ad revenue to roughly double to around $3B this year. For me, this quarter is less about proving Netflix can grow. It is more about proving how much more profitable this business can become as it keeps scaling. Double-digit revenue growth is great. But operating income growing around 30% while margins expand by roughly 500 basis points YoY is what really stands out to me.

Author: TradeWithInsight
Text: $NFLX reports Tuesday after the close. $TSLA and $META report Wednesday after the close. When a company reports after the close, the stock reacts in after-hours trading and most of the move shows up as a gap at the next open. Options price that event in ahead of time. Implied volatility climbs into the report and drops right after it. That drop is called IV crush. It's why calls can lose value even when the stock goes up the next day. The move has to beat what the options already priced in.

The margin guide is 33.2% vs 28.2% a year ago, though that year-ago number took a Brazilian tax charge that knocked more than 5 points off it. Underlying margin is closer to flat. Targets kept coming down into the print anyway. Wedbush cut to 90 from 105 on Friday and kept Outperform, BMO went to 125 from 135, and the stock closed Friday at 70.53, down 2.9%.
